newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-SLOVAKIA TURN TABLES ON FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-SLOVAKIA TURN TABLES ON FRANCE.

text.p: Three goals in less than four minutes early in the second period helped Slovakia turn the tables on France and win 5-3 at the world ice hockey championship on Monday.
France got off to a brilliant start, leading the group A match 2-0 after little more than five minutes through goals by defender Brian Arnaud and centre forward Cristian Pouget.
Slovak captain Zdenko Ciger pulled one back in the eighth minute, but France dominated the action throughout the first period.
Slovakia found their composure in the second period and Roman Stantien equalised in the 23rd minute on a low shot from a tight angle to the left.
Just 69 seconds later, the Slovaks struck again through Roman Kontsek.
Francois Gravel, who replaced French goalkeeper Christobal Huet, had a nightmare start, letting in a shot from Jan Pardavy after just one minute and 12 seconds on the ice.
Stantien added another for good measure in the 37th minute to make the score 5-2.
"We scored too few goals considering the chances we had," said Slovak head coach Jozef Golonka.
Arnaud's 58th minute goal for France came too late to put any pressure on the Slovaks, who moved into third place in the group behind the Czech Republic and Russia.
France and Germany are at the bottom of the group, with two defeats in as many games.
